blocks.text: American biologist, Thomas Hunt Morgan, studied two traits in Drosophila i.e., wing length and abdomen width. He observed that allele for long wings (L) is dominant over short or vestigial wing (l). Similarly, allele for broad abdomen (B) is dominant over narrow abdomen (b). Morgan did the following cross in drosophila;
Then, he crossed two of F1 flies. The results are shown in the following figure:
Explanation of Result: According to law of independent assortment, the F2 generation should have the following 9:3:3:1 ratio:
But Morgan observed only parental combinations in F2. There were 3/4 flies with long wings-broad abdomen and 1/4 with vestigial wings-narrow abdomen.

blocks.alt: A cross drawn with flies and their chromosome pairs in circles. Parents: a long-winged, broad-abdomen fly LLBB (both chromosomes carry L and B) x a vestigial-winged, narrow-abdomen fly llbb. All gametes carry L-B or l-b. F1: two long-winged, broad-abdomen LlBb flies are crossed; each forms gametes L-B and l-b. F2 genotypes: 1/4 LLBB, 1/4 LlBb, 1/4 LlBb, 1/4 llbb. F2 phenotypes: 3/4 long wing, broad abdomen and 1/4 vestigial wing, narrow abdomen.
blocks.caption: Figure 18.10: Gene linkage in Drosophila (original drawing after the textbook's Figure 18.10).
blocks.long_description: Labels: Parents, Gametes (All), F1, Gametes, F2 Genotype, F2 Phenotype, Long wing, broad abdomen, Vestigial wing, narrow abdomen.

blocks.text: From this data, Morgan concluded that the genes for wing length and abdomen width were located on the same chromosome and they did no assort independently.
